title: Repair task tracking with event-driven analysis
description:
# Event-driven progress repair and QA plan

## 1. Authority, scope and implementation gate

User decisions, in order:
1. Treat this session as QA and convert the observed failure into regression tests.
2. Fix the bugs; no new feature work until testing and bug-squashing is complete.
3. Replace interval polling with event-driven analysis. Finalized messages drive task updates; relevant tool evidence drives health. Remove obsolete interval controls.
4. Create a detailed plan, then dependency-ordered Beads, and only then start implementation.

This packet is the detailed implementation plan for issue `pi-progress-barroot-82j`, not the independent-advisory plan. Advisory steering, new health signals, other providers, child-agent monitoring and generated task labels remain OUT of scope. The old advisory defaults/interval proposal does not govern this repair.

**Gate:** No new production implementation until this plan, testing.md, slices.md and the complete Beads dependency graph exist and are checked. The worker is explicitly held read-only. The only existing production patch is the already-authorized sentence-parser repair, made before the new planning gate; preserve it without expanding it. Main owns tests, Beads, validation, acceptance and final publication.

## 2. Baseline and established evidence

- Accepted release/bookmark: `afdbee79` (qmi/jks delivered).
- Committed QA tests: `afb62c31` (fresh messages starve behind replay) and `019d82ad` (lost spans, actual scope-admission latency, real-Jev QA replay).
- Working change at planning start: `yyyussuw`; parser-only modification in `src/sources/trajectory.ts` plus additional main-owned, not-yet-validated safety tests in `__tests__/fresh-session.test.ts`.
- Screenshot displayed historical response task from source `4e9449e0`, with unresolved scope, despite new reading request `74093355`.
- Actual v3 checkpoints show fresh-state reset, old-history replay, and the reading request becoming unresolved almost twelve minutes after submission. Checkpoint versions do not prove the exact loaded source revision.
- Deterministic replay: without backlog all five QA user messages reach selection; with 40/520 old messages they do not reach selection in the next normal cycle. Two additional tests require actual replacement scope admission, not merely a priority selection call.
- Real Jev replay before parser fix: 5 attempts, 6,300 input /575 output tokens. Selection recognized reading request at probability .97, but classification omitted offsets15:188 containing the request. Regex sentence splitting discarded text before embedded periods in `.agents/.../plan.md`.
- Parser-only correction preserves internal punctuation and exact offsets. Focused trajectory suite18/18; subsequent real production replay passes with7 attempts,8,920 input/1,021 output. Repair total so far12 attempts,15,220 input/1,596 output. This does not validate the future event scheduler.
- Previous accepted release evidence:163 unit+10 integration,15 live (before last display-only snapshot-timing fix). Do not present those as post-event-repair results.

Supporting diagnosis and raw bounded live artifacts remain in `../20260919T072656--diagnose-user-message-reassessment__active/`. Only sanitized fixtures belong in committed tests.

## 3. Required behavior

### R1 — Message-driven reassessment
Every newly persisted, eligible user message enters Jev-driven task-scope reassessment. It need not create a task: add, same, revise, replace goal, context/no-change and honest ambiguity are distinct outcomes. Questions and requests for explanation/reading are work when Jev judges them as such. An assistant message may establish a grounded plan or report task lifecycle changes; it is not automatically a new task or completion proof.

Fresh user input must not wait for an arbitrarily long historical replay to be considered. Scope must actually update when the bounded semantic transaction authorizes it. Merely evaluating and caching selection while leaving the task list stuck does not satisfy this requirement.

### R2 — Event-driven health
Relevant captured tool evidence or changed task/evidence identity schedules health work. Tool activity never owns reported completion. Duplicate tool/message callbacks must not duplicate calls. Retained task cards remain presentation-only and keep all five labels frozen at health admission.

### R3 — No periodic analysis or interval API
Keep `/progress`, `/progress on`, `/progress off`. Remove `/progress interval`, interval help/status/widget wording, runtime interval state and checkpoint interval data. No alias, inert compatibility property or hidden polling mode. Invalid old commands show the new usage without changing monitoring state.

No traffic or task-list mutation from redraws, unchanged branch snapshots, clocks advancing during idle, or monitoring's own entries. The timestamp remains the last actual HTTP dispatch, including failures.

### R4 — Bounded, ordered and conservative
One Jev request in flight. Preserve pinned `jev-1.13.0`, existing request/question/response/deadline limits and confidence gates. No keyword classification, arbitrary first-task current selection, threshold weakening or test-specific production exceptions.

Bound memory and per-request work. Finite queued observations must drain without requiring another user message and without an arbitrary lifetime/request cap stranding them. Do not mint a new three-request allowance for each callback. Calls are driven by unfinished valid semantic transitions, not elapsed time. Higher throughput relative to15s polling is disclosed and measured, not described as free.

### R5 — Safe persistence and lifecycle
OFF, session shutdown and branch/session changes invalidate pending callbacks and abort dispatch appropriately. Validated durable decisions remain durable; ephemeral fresh work does not become authority through serialization. Old reports cannot complete a newer replacement goal, even after reload. Repeated events and restored accepted chunks cannot rebill or apply the same transition twice.

## 4. Architecture: small event-driven controller

Reuse `Monitor`, `Conversation`, `AnalysisScheduler`, `JevGateway` and the existing ledger/scope/report reducers. Do not fork Monitor or add a generic event bus/framework. New helpers only where they isolate a concrete boundary.

### 4.1 Observation and host persistence boundary

Candidate signals (to verify against installed/pinned Pi in slice E1):

| Signal | Work it may schedule | Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Finalized user/assistant `message_end` | Reconcile persisted branch; enqueue unseen sources/reports | Stored exact entry/ref/hash, never raw event text |
| `agent_settled` and a verified post-persistence hook | Catch final entries missed by event-before-persistence ordering | Active branch originals |
| Matched tool execution end | Update evidence; schedule health if identity changed | Existing bounded tool adapters and links |
| Start/restore/ON/tree | Rehydrate canonical state; enqueue valid outstanding evidence | Valid checkpoint plus live source validation |
| Widget/help/redraw | Display only | None |

`message_end` also covers other roles; filter event eligibility structurally. Do not use toolResult/custom/monitor messages as conversation task authority. Event handlers never await Jev.

Pi may deliver a notification before its entry is persisted. E1 must demonstrate a supported way to observe the durable original during a long-running turn, not just after the agent settles. A coalesced local deferred read may be used only if host tests establish its guarantee; one microtask is not assumed sufficient. Test delayed persistence and other async handlers. If the host contract cannot provide this, stop and resolve the exact limitation before claiming every user message is captured. No perpetual branch polling substitute.

### 4.2 Serialized drain and fairness

A relevant event marks evidence dirty and requests one coalesced drain. Duplicate requests while a drain is scheduled/running do not start another. At each boundary, refresh valid state, choose one pending semantic operation, and dispatch only if enabled, generation-valid and provider-eligible. Response admission may unlock the next phase; continue via a yielded local scheduling turn until quiescent, blocked by service backoff, invalidated, or out of valid bounded work.

Use explicit states equivalent to idle / scheduled / running / waiting-retry / stopped. Avoid overlapping booleans with contradictory ownership. Cached/admitted/no-op transitions must also make measurable progress or stop; no CPU/cache spin.

When fresh user work and historical work coexist, reserve opportunities for both: no more than two consecutive request dispatches from one class while the other has runnable work. A fresh stage must be selected within three eligible dispatch opportunities after it becomes runnable (excluding a request already in flight and documented service backoff). At least one historical operation runs in the same bound if both stay pending. A small deterministic selector is sufficient; do not recreate interval cycles under a new name.

Preserve order within a burst of distinct fresh user entries. An actionable candidate advances through selection, classification and scope without allowing a later user turn to erase it. Coalesce notifications and identical request identities, not user-message history. If capacity is exceeded, expose pending/coverage limits and retain replayable references; never silently drop a turn or claim no-change.

### 4.3 Fresh task-scope admission, not cosmetic priority

Keep exact id/hash references for newly observed user messages even beyond the normal512-entry history window. Reuse existing candidate selection/classification requests and deterministic reducers. A cached early decision is only reusable for the same complete request identity and epoch; selection alone has no ledger authority.

The first bounded early-admission path accepts only a complete single-entry, single-chunk transaction whose existing Jev scope judgment passes all confidence/coverage checks as `new-goal`, with all candidate relations `new`. Then use existing scope application to retire old included tasks without calling them done, and commit an exact boundary reference. Clear stale queued/in-flight work and proofs only to the extent authorized by this new-goal cutover. Later history must not overwrite the new denominator or apply earlier completion to it.

`continue`, `same`, `revised`, ambiguous, incomplete, oversize/multi-chunk, invalid refs and low-confidence outcomes cannot authorize jumping unsettled history. Preserve them for normal chronological reconciliation; expose pending/unknown rather than falsely claiming an update. Already-clear chronological continuations continue to work normally.

No-ledger startup must still consider fresh user messages promptly. A grounded first proposal may initialize scope only through validated source/task semantics; skipping unsettled earlier history needs an explicit semantic replacement boundary, not “most recent message wins.” Tests cover startup without an established ledger separately from replacement of an existing one.

Pending fresh work and replay must not both bill the same selection/classification concurrently. Cache sharing uses exact request identities; changed preceding context is not a cache hit. The cutover source/hash, applied enums, scope revision and report/discovery boundaries must survive reload as canonical, bounded state. Do not advance a durable cursor for a provisional result.

### 4.4 Service failures and retry wakeups

Retain current classification of permanent/transient errors until a demonstrated defect requires change; no second inference lane is introduced. Expose the gateway's next eligible retry deadline through a narrow read-only API if necessary.

Only pending, retryable work may arm a one-shot wakeup. Respect Retry-After/current backoff, the existing bounded failure burst and cooldown. One wakeup owner; new evidence must not bypass it. OFF/epoch change clears it. A cancelled/empty queue has no timer. Failed or cached work cannot create an immediate re-dispatch loop. No generic maintenance interval.

Beads enrichment remains read-only, optional and non-authoritative. Refresh on lifecycle and relevant observation/admission boundaries, coalescing concurrent reads. An idle export edit alone need not refresh until another relevant event or explicit ON; document this rather than retaining polling merely for enrichment.

### 4.5 Controls, UI and checkpoint boundary

Public controls: `/progress`, `on`, `off` only. Help/widget retain meaningful activity, pending/catch-up/unknown/service state, actual last-call freshness and usage. Replace interval text with an honest event-driven state. No expanded inspector or steering controls.

Remove interval from the persisted shape and bump the strict checkpoint schema (planned v4). Reject/rebuild obsolete v3 and malformed v4; no migration or inert interval compatibility. Rebuild is visible and may cost calls, so provide accurate reload/manual-test instructions. Fresh-user priority must work while rebuilding. Keep reference-only privacy, bounded journals, digests as corruption detection rather than authentication, and immutable memory-only retained cards.

## 5. Implementation sequence and ownership

See slices.md for E0–E5 and testing.md for exact gates. Every slice has an observable test/demo, main-authored reds before behavior changes, and a conventional jj commit. Do not create/switch branches. One tracked-code writer at a time; explicit main/worker handoff around test edits. Worker cannot modify tests, Beads, configuration or run paid calls. Main handles shared quality gates and publication.

Beads are created only after this packet is complete. Each ticket carries a portable description and acceptance conditions, not merely a link to ignored plans. Parent82j stays open until full repair accepted. Do not close the bug after parser success alone.

## 6. Validation and release

- Convert old cadence assertions deliberately: event arrival -> bounded dispatch ordering -> actual scope/health state. Do not delete response/current, atomicity, cost or lifecycle assertions simply because interval APIs disappear.
- Run format -> check -> unit/integration; package dry-run; isolated actual Pi event/persistence tests with fake transport and zero outbound network.
- Run focused real-Jev QA after semantic/structural changes, then existing qmi/jks semantic regression corpus. Use separate bounded invocations where a combined suite would exceed a cap; count failures and retries. Initial focused cap24 attempts, existing suite cap64; no automatic retries or parallel uncoordinated evaluation. | Area | Required cases | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Source spans | Exact QA request; dotted path; URL/query; decimal/version; optional chaining/nonterminal punctuation; Unicode; list/fenced behavior | No lost instruction; exact source slices; no invented text |

| Idle | No new events; repeated redraw/help/branch snapshots; large fake-clock advances | Zero extra calls or analysis polling |
| Drain | Multi-phase source/classification/scope/report; cached result; bounded history paging; no-op/error results | Finite work drains without a new event; no cache/CPU spin or arbitrary budget stop |

| Cancellation | OFF/stop/tree/reload mid-selection/classification/scope; delayed completion callback | No late admission or unintended new calls; invalidation releases flight ownership |
| Retry | 429 Retry-After, timeout/5xx, permanent error, cached failure, new events during backoff | One pending-only wakeup; no bypass/spin; OFF clears; idle has none |

title: Deliver automatic plan-v2 monitor through V6
description:
Deliver the automatic plan-v2 product as one human-testable batch, replacing the existing manual V1–V3 workflow and adding V4, V5 and V6.

Product contract:
- Installed extension is ON by default. TYPESAFE_API_KEY is mandatory; missing/blank or rejected credentials produce one clear error and OFF, not a local-only fallback.
- Actual TypeSafe Jev calls are the sole semantic runtime. No general-purpose/reasoning LLM, generated task descriptions, generated summaries or model-written labels. Code owns task IDs, arithmetic, state and score/Choice display mappings.
- Commands only: /progress on, off, interval <seconds>. Bare command gives usage/state. No consent, details, source/Apply, enable/pause/resume, manual scope/current-task selection, or compatibility aliases.
- Automatically extract task-like spans from actual active-branch conversation, reconcile evolving scope/stable identities, infer current task, and apply explicit done/reopen/cancel reports in lineage order. Percentage is reported completed / active discovered tasks, never effort or correctness.
- Proposed operational defaults from plan v2:60s cycle interval, configurable5–86400s; at most3 serial requests/cycle, single flight,10s deadline,24KiB request/20questions. No repeated calls for unchanged successful evidence, fixed15s dispatch override, or60-attempt lifetime wall. Autonomous bounded retry/backoff, not a resume command.
- Preserve passive main-session behavior. No agent message injection, tool replacement, project commands/tests, issue mutation, child monitoring or sibling evidence.
- V4: automatic grounded Beads identity/context enrichment, not a source picker or whole-backlog counter. V5: new-red applicability plus distinct Not needed/Reported red/Observed red. V6: criterion-linked implementation evidence, separate from reported completion. V7 temporal meaningful-progress/stuck/drift is excluded from this requested batch.

Implementation discipline: main authors failing behavior tests before scoped writers; writers never edit tests. Serial working increments, one production writer/cwd. Use jj conventional commits, no new branches. Keep ignored task artifacts, Bun/Biome/TypeScript/Knip/Vitest and make format/check/test. Remove obsolete code and checkpoint schema without compatibility migrations. One bounded independent full-batch review after integration; timeout is not approval.

Delivery requires actual no-command Pi+Jev demonstration and bounded live evaluation, not just injected transport tests. Record usage/errors/limitations; no uncontrolled billable sweep. Detailed plan remains ignored at .agents/plans/20260918T154145--replan-automatic-conversation-monitor__planning/plan_v2.md; child issue bodies are self-contained.

Supersedes old manual-workflow delivery epic pi-progress-barroot-1t2. Its completed work is reusable history, not evidence the new product is delivered. Old independent review timed out without verdict.

Only on/off/interval controls. No extra LLM or intervention. Deterministic and bounded real-Jev validation, full-batch review, packaged user-test checkpoint. V7 excluded.

title: Plan-v2 step 1: Automatic Jev progress loop
description:
Replace manual V1 startup with a minimal working automatic conversation->real Jev->reported progress loop. This is an end-to-end visible increment, not merely a default-on empty widget.

Implement: startup ON with TYPESAFE_API_KEY; missing/blank key one error and OFF; rejected credentials error+OFF. Only /progress on|off|interval <seconds>, bare usage/state. Remove consent/source/Apply/details/enable/pause/resume flows and aliases. No manual checklist/current-task setup. On/off idempotent; off aborts/invalidate pending responses, stops collection/network/timers and hides widget. Preserve current-session controls over reload; new sessions default ON, tree must not undo OFF. Interval controls analysis-cycle starts (default60s,5–86400s), including while OFF. No unchanged-history calls. One valid short natural-language request must discover tasks and then explicit completion automatically.

Use existing fixed TypeSafe endpoint/pinned Jev gateway and typed source spans; no general-purpose LLM or fake/local-only runtime. Keep ledger report arithmetic independent from assessment. Delete manual checklist-only runtime paths; relocate shared constants rather than retain dead modules. Version new checkpoint schema, ignore obsolete manual-source checkpoints and rebuild from active history; no migration layer. Reuse useful safety code, not obsolete UX.

Likely areas: src/index.ts, core/monitor.ts, ui/commands.ts, widget.ts, analysis/gateway.ts, sources/conversation.ts; package description/README must describe actual stage accurately.

Main-owned tests first: no-key/blank-key/off, key present without consent, short two-task request and explicit report without commands, invalid/repeated toggles and intervals, timer replacement, no calls on redraw/empty unchanged session, no agent/tool/exec effects. Child implementers may run, not edit, tests. Real endpoint required in runtime; injected transport exists only in tests. Full live quality gate belongs to final delivery ticket, not an unbounded call during this step.

Done when ordinary short conversation yields a reported fraction automatically, controls/key failures work, obsolete manual command paths are absent, and available format/check/test gates pass. Large-history and complex scope guarantees arrive in dependent steps, not claimed here.

title: Plan-v2 step 2: Incremental history and exact task spans
description:
Extend the working automatic loop to arbitrary-length current-branch history without lifetime-prefix truncation or candidate-shortlist starvation.

Read finalized entries from getBranch, never sibling/child sessions. Account for message_end preceding persistence; timer/settled observations capture originals. Cursor = committed entry ID/hash/span offset, not fetched/dispatched position. Start bounded chronological catch-up when no valid checkpoint; append new arrivals without restarting in-flight discovery. Initial working bounds:32 visible messages/window,256KiB text,24KiB serialized requests,20questions/request; windows roll indefinitely. References survive RAM eviction and rehydrate from current-branch originals. Deduplicate live/persisted entries, own metadata and overlap. Distinguish window absence from genuinely unavailable originals. Automatically recover available ancestors/checkpoints; no source reselection. Irrecoverable gaps remain visible; later explicitly self-contained goal may establish a new trustworthy scope without inventing old status.

Candidate enumeration is mechanical: Markdown blocks/list items, sentence segmentation and proposed clause boundaries with exact offsets. Keep whole-span/child alternatives and source context (quotes/code/examples); Jev decides actionable task boundaries, including structured lists. Never count both overlapping parent and children, never split every 'and' into tasks, never synthesize task wording or use another LLM. Overlong messages become offset-linked subchunks; indivisible evidence overflow is visible Unknown, not silent clipping. Use all bounded candidate batches over time, not a permanent first12 shortlist. No task admission from regex alone.

Likely areas: sources/trajectory.ts, candidates.ts, conversation controller/cursor/checkpoints. Preserve active-branch provenance and privacy filtering. Deferred V5 adds narrow tool-fact adapters; generic tool bodies remain excluded as task/status authority.

Main tests first: >512 entries/>256KiB lifetime history reaches tail; oversized message continues after restart; new arrivals don't reset pending work; compound prose versus 'compare authentication and authorization'; wrapped bullets, numbered examples, quotes, parent/child overlap, aborted messages; private/system/thinking/sibling exclusion; own checkpoints cause no feedback loop; recoverable versus irrecoverable gaps. No paid calls for structural tests.

Done when visible catching-up state advances to current automatic task progress on long replay with no lost/duplicate observations, bounded working state/requests and passing gates.
acceptance_criteria: Long history and oversized messages reach latest evidence with bounded windows, exact offsets and committed cursor; no permanent prefix/shortlist, restart starvation, parent-child double count, sibling or private evidence. Automatic recovery and tests/gates pass.
close_reason: Rolling bounded history reaches tail; exact-offset candidate subchunks remove permanent shortlist and regex-only admission

title: Plan-v2 step 3: Evolving scope and ordered task reports
description:
Make automatic discovery maintain an evolving goal-scoped ledger, not repeatedly auto-Apply a newer plan and erase status.

Jev classifies exact supplied task spans and relates mentions to existing task IDs/earlier candidates/new work/uncertain. Give task meanings and acceptance context, never IDs alone. Local code owns stable IDs, versions, scope, evidence refs and transitions. Repeated paraphrases do not multiply denominator. Exact Beads IDs can later strengthen identity. Similar wording alone never transfers done; semantic same-task matches require same work/boundaries. If requests partition comparison candidates, no match in one shortlist is not proof of a new task. Materially expanded work gets a revised task scope with old completion inapplicable; ambiguous identity is unresolved, not silently merged/newly counted.

Infer current task from actual user direction/assistant present-work statements, never first unchecked. Active denominator concerns current conversational goal, not whole session/backlog. Add new actual work, preserve legitimate repeated evidence, archive old scope on clear new user goal without marking it done. Cancelled is not done; remove from active denominator only when conversation removes work from scope. Quotes/alternatives/hypotheticals do not become commitments. Unreliable denominator means Unknown, not guessed percentage or a manual picker.

Interpret explicit done/reopen/cancel/in-progress reports in entry/span order. Support task introduction plus completion within the same logical observation. Chunk task questions under20/24KiB, apply only complete validated transaction against its starting ledger revision. Reopen must survive batching. Cursor advances on committed outcomes, not dispatch; service failure never skips evidence. Valid ambiguity can be retained for future context without blocking the whole queue. Admission binds session/branch/scope/task revision/cursor. Status proofs survive bounded inspector-free history eviction. Health can never write completion.

Main tests first: paraphrase duplicate, genuine additional work, revised completed task, current-task ambiguity, competing/new goal, cancel vs removal, done then reopen across chunks, 23+ task atomic report, introduction+done same chunk, quote/intentions, ambiguous correction, stale response after branch/scope changes, replay exactly once, proof restore after eviction. Separate candidate recall failures from Jev identity errors in later live gate.

Done when ordinary evolving conversation gives stable automatic tasks/current task and correct reported fractions with explicit uncertainty, no source control, preserved order/provenance, and passing gates.
acceptance_criteria: Stable automatic identities/current task; paraphrases vs new/revised work resolved safely; ordered atomic done/reopen/cancel including same-chunk task creation; no guessed denominator or health completion writes; replay/branch/restore tests pass.
close_reason: Semantic scope relations preserve identities, invalidate revised completion, infer current task safely, and archive clear new goals; ordered reports remain atomic

title: Plan-v2 step 4: Automatic health and resilient runtime
description:
Complete replacement V1–V3 automatic task signals, autonomous failure handling and lifecycle resilience on the same working conversation loop. No consent/manual task/source UI returns.

Feed grounded automatic goal/current-task/owned criteria into existing Jev clarity Score0–3 and acceptance Choice rubrics. Missing current task or essential evidence is Unknown, not score0. Refresh semantic assessments only when relevant state changes; successful identical input and rendering do not create requests. Local pure display mapping: [0,1)=unclear,[1,2)=partly clear,[2,3)=mostly clear,exact3=clear; missing/nonfinite/out-of-range=unknown. 2.7 renders 'Requirements: mostly clear', not2.7/3; do not round first. Choice labels, timestamps and status text also local. No additional model call to write labels, rationale or summaries. Confidence is distinct from rubric score. Health never updates report ledger.

Runtime scheduling: default60s analysis-cycle starts, interval command5–86400s; startup/on may catch up immediately; up to3 serial requests/cycle,10s deadline,24KiB/20questions,128KiB responses, one flight. Pending work carries across cycles. Remove inherited15s dispatch override and60-attempt enablement budget. Fair turns for extraction/reports/health, not continual cancellation/starvation. User-only changes and last idle-turn reports process on timer. No evidence=no new calls.

Missing/rejected key is error+OFF. Transient network/5xx/429/timeout failures retain cursor and visibly stale/as-of progress; exponential backoff at least configured interval, honor longer Retry-After. At most3 attempts/burst, attempts count toward cycle limits; then5min cooldown and one probe before a new bounded burst. New evidence does not evade global backoff. Malformed/oversized results reject atomically, bounded retry/cooldown; permanent request/model configuration errors report+OFF. No resume/enable. Off aborts before late-result cleanup and stops collection; on resumes current-branch catch-up. Reload/tree/session changes invalidate outstanding generations and revalidate checkpoint refs/status proofs. Restore controls without accidentally re-enabling OFF on tree navigation. Old manual checkpoints ignored, no migration.

Main tests first: all score boundary/invalid cases and zero network on rendering; separate ledger authority; real gateway wiring with test-only injected transport; budget beyond60 successful requests; low interval honored, max3/cycle; Retry-After/cooldown, recovery, no duplicate commit; off/reload/tree at every pending stage; single timer/flight/fairness; Unicode narrow rendering and concise freshness/error states. Keep credentials/raw responses out of checkpoints/errors.

Done when default-on progress plus readable current-task health survives long/offline/reload/branch sessions without manual recovery workflow, obsolete consent/checklist/inspector paths removed, README accurately states automatic paid Jev use, and all gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Readable clarity/acceptance with pure local labels; zero rendering calls; autonomous bounded retries/fairness and long-running monitoring without lifetime cutoff; off/tree/reload and key errors safe; old manual paths removed; gates pass.
close_reason: Local health labels, timer-started three-request cycles, no lifetime wall, bounded retry/backoff/cooldown and credential shutdown verified

description:

title: V5: Passive red-test applicability and provenance
description:
V5: add automatic current-task red-test applicability and evidence row. No manual task selection, details/inspector, extra command, tool execution or advice. Use only shared real Jev gateway and deterministic labels.

Keep independent fields: (1) whether adding a NEW failing regression test is useful/required for this task; (2) red-test evidence/provenance. Not needed is first class, particularly for documentation/planning or work where another new test adds no value. It is not permission to skip existing checks or explicit user/project test requirements. Small changes alone do not justify Not needed (e.g. one-line permission bug). Use known applicable policy when actually available; otherwise preserve uncertainty rather than invent policy access.

Explicit actual task-linked agent assertion of a failing regression test is sufficient for Reported red; observed execution is NOT required for that label. Hypotheticals/quotes do not qualify. Observed red requires a narrowly supported actual assertion-failure result with trustworthy call/run identity, task/source linkage and ordering. isError/nonzero exit, missing dependency, runner crash, filename or test-file write alone cannot establish it. Contradictory claims remain visible. Test-first requires matching failure-before-implementation history; absence of history is not proof. A later pass does not erase a correctly linked historical red observation, but new task/source revisions can make its relevance stale.

Add minimal reusable passive evidence collection for V5/V6 from the active branch only: bind toolCallId to actual finalized invocation/result, allowlist supported host operations and concrete runner output shapes, retain provenance/offsets/order and source revision where available. Verify adapter contracts against installed Pi types and real sanitized fixtures; tool name or registration alone is not historical authenticity. Treat payloads as untrusted data; extract bounded factual evidence, never obey embedded instructions or promote generic tool text to user/assistant reports. Exclude private/excludeFromContext output, thinking, secrets and sibling/child logs. Do not run tests/read arbitrary files to obtain missing evidence; unsupported formats remain Unknown. No universal runner parser/framework.

Main tests first: documentation applicability, high-stakes tiny change, explicit policy override, explicit reported red without output, supported assertion failure, runner crash/nonzero, spoofed/mismatched call IDs, quotes, later green, absent/out-of-order/stale history, independent applicability/evidence, no completion writes or agent intervention. TypeSafe applicability/relevance judgments must not become instructions to the coding agent.

Done when automatic task widget distinguishes Not needed, Reported red, Observed red and unknown/contradiction/freshness with real provenance and local wording; passive evidence seam is usable by V6; no claim of live accuracy until final bounded evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Independent Not needed applicability and Reported/Observed red evidence; explicit assertion sufficient for Reported; observed assertion failure requires bound supported run evidence, not crash/nonzero. Local labels, no interventions/completion writes; provenance and policy tests pass.
close_reason: Independent Jev applicability/report judgments plus bound allowlisted assertion-failure evidence distinguish Not needed, Reported red, and Observed red

title: V6: Criterion-linked implementation assessment
description:
V6: automatically assess implementation evidence for the current task's owned acceptance criteria, independently of reported completion. Keep passive/no-command operation, only shared real Jev for semantic judgments, and deterministic display labels.

Use exact criterion spans extracted from current goal/task conversation and narrowly supported passive code/edit/test observations collected in V5. Keep source/task revision, entry/call/run identity, chronology and coverage per criterion. Agent self-report remains report evidence, not independent proof implementation satisfies criteria. No workspace-wide crawling, hidden builds/tests, shell execution, code generation or general-purpose LLM. Unsupported/missing source linkage is Unknown, not fabricated observation.

Ask independent per-criterion typed Choices (supports/contradicts/insufficient evidence) over relevant bounded evidence; batch under existing request/cycle limits. Do not infer complete criteria from a truncated prefix. Local aggregation: any current contradiction -> contradicted; incomplete/missing/stale essential coverage -> unverified or partial according to supported criteria; only full known criteria coverage with supporting current evidence can display 'appears complete'. These labels remain assessments, never proof of arbitrary correctness. No multiplied confidence or numeric percent masquerading as probability the whole task is correct.

## Approved changes superseding revision 2

1. Reconciliation asks actual status of pending tasks, not to implement more work. Response MUST enter existing task pipeline and update board when supported; Jev/extraction calls may be needed. Zero Jev applies to deterministic trigger, not response processing. Truthful blocked status need not change board. Do not force completion or silently relax existing thresholds.
2. Next independent agent run may nudge same unchanged pending board. Run solely answering advisory cannot rearm. Genuine external/user input wins in mixed runs. Replace cross-run stable-board dedupe with per-eligible-run opportunity and duplicate event protection.
3. Deadline = authoritative independent agent settlement + 60_000ms. Board ready at +20s sends at +60s; board ready at +80s sends then. Same-run semantic processing refreshes rows, does not cancel/restart deadline. Never send against unfinished task analysis.
4. Owner accepts no guaranteed retraction after sendMessage invocation. Known OFF/start/navigation cancels before invocation. No private queue APIs or silent host rewrite.
5. NO advisory ON/OFF, preference, configurable capability toggles or per-session opt-in. Extension master ON means progress + supported nudges; master OFF means neither. Remove independent new-session/legacy advisory OFF rollout. Technical safety gates internal; they must not become user-facing configuration. Ship capabilities incrementally after tests/host checks/review.
6. Evidence gate is correctness, not extra user workflow. Question itself is not completion/new task evidence; actual answer may be. Preserve genuine status claims, no duplicate tasks from copied labels. Do not turn this into speculative plagiarism architecture; demonstrate smallest sufficient current-source contract. Scope-changing proof/schema prerequisites must be explicit, not invented or silently modified.
7. Test advice REUSES existing fresh Jev not-needed decision. Trigger WHEN agent starts writing a new red test for that task; no duplicate necessity inference by default. Exact requested message: "Task X does not need a failing test, as the test will not provide any long-term value. Please directly start with the implementation instead." This supersedes started-action-is-missed suppression. Agent decides response, no extension cancellation/undo. Existing explicit user/repository requirement veto remains. Exact detection and task binding is investigation work; do not guess from focus/name alone. Do not claim existing typed result proves long-term-value rationale without inspecting actual rubric.
8. Review advice triggers AFTER premature review starts. Exact requested message: "Reviewing the work done so far is premature. Please cancel the review and continue with the implementation. It is better to review the work when a bigger chunk of it has been completed." Main agent handles cancellation, extension never does. Explicit review requirements/security/blocker protection remains. One proven structured adapter initially; investigate actual launch schemas, no shell/name heuristics or child transcript mining.
9. Per-distinct-attempt correction, NOT once per task/checkpoint. Duplicate tool events/continued edits same attempt do not repeat; genuinely new attempt can nudge again. Jev suitable for same-attempt/new-attempt/unknown classification; deterministic exact event dedupe and freshness still required. Validate examples/thresholds; unknown abstains.
10. Bounded inputs approved, but WHOLE INCLUDED TASK BOARD goes to Jev for parallel task-bound judgments, not only focus. No arbitrary truncation; activity must bind to task(s), not automatically to all rows. Bounded relevant policy/conversation/activity and previous-attempt context; no wholesale tool outputs/file contents/shell commands/child transcripts. Explicitly investigate whether supported metadata is enough for detection. No duplicate per-task calls or delayed batch cadence.
11. RETRY uncertain/failed delivery preferred over lost nudge; occasional duplicates explicitly acceptable. Remove strict at-most-once reserve/no-retry tradeoff. Recheck relevance/master/session/current attempt before retry. Known delivery/response should stop delivery retries; unchanged board is not send failure. Exact finite retry/backoff/reload recovery contract remains implementation design; don't silently interpret this as authorizing all restored timers or unlimited loops. At-least-once attempt policy is not guaranteed delivery.
12. Accepted order: reconciliation -> test corrections -> review corrections. Each capability deterministic tests, real Pi delivery checks, independent review; Jev semantics bounded paid evaluation. Master ON enables accepted capabilities; no extra switch; unfinished capabilities don't block accepted ones.

description:
# Main decisions / final plan amendments

Planner recovery cfb43cf6 completed; draft copied into this task folder. Main approves the hybrid architecture with the following authoritative amendments. User explicitly authorizes complete plan→portable detailed Beads→sequential implementation→automated/live/review gates→manual testing.

## Keep the current product working while replacing it

Do not delete the old semantic modules in slice1 and strand all other tests/features until slice4. Build the new bounded observation transaction as an isolated, fully exercised core vertical first. Current production extension remains unchanged until the cutover slice; this is temporary development staging, not a shipped feature flag, fallback or compatibility contract.

Final sequence (four implementation slices plus acceptance/publication):
- H1: New task state, canonical message helpers, whole-message gate, strict grounded additions, selected-model seam, independent focused completion, transaction runner. Fresh-session core end-to-end tests prove requested CI/parallel/newly-completed behavior. Keep current runtime and its tests green.
- H2: Complete revise/archive/restore semantics, per-task assessment/provenance, strictv5 persistence, partial phase/chunk journal, idempotency, bounded labels/events. Core restart/off-on transaction tests. Existing runtime still intact.
- H3: Integrate atomic host/monitor/UI/health cutover with one-flight lifecycle and public host-selected-model adapter. Migrate main-owned tests before released source work, remove obsolete semantic modules and dormant paths in the same slice. Existing five health meanings, Beads safety and command surface remain. All available gates green before closing.
- H4: Long-session finite drain/bounds/failure hardening and real supported-host proofs. Main restores equivalent regression coverage for historical lost prefix/suffix/chronology/cache bugs against new implementation. This closes remaining coverage, not permission to ship a broken H3.
- H5 (acceptance, not another feature slice): bounded actual-provider fixtures, independent whole-unpublished-batch review, fixes with main tests, docs/disclosure/package/version support, final commit/publication and manual test handoff.

## Scope and authority

Accepted change: generated grounded labels and selected-LLM decomposition supersede old Jev-only/no-generated-label requirements. Preserve confidence.5/probability.8 and pinnedJev. Generatedlabels persist in strictv5 (240chars), but raw context/prompts/provider outputs/keys do not. Latest per-task derived assessment values/provenance are allowed in v5, not raw provider envelopes. Persist dispatch timestamps/usage as specifically disclosed v5 change. No v4 migration.

Focus is presentation/health selection ONLY. It MUST NOT automatically authorize task attribution of a tool call. Keep tools unlinked when no independent task/revision linkage exists; Observed red/implementation remain unknown or unsupported rather than borrowing focus as evidence authority. Requirements/acceptance/Reported red can use bounded task-local conversational evidence. Do not secretly introduce a new active-task classifier or claim tools prove completion. Main tests must enforce focus≠execution ownership.

Fresh-over-history priority/early cutover is deliberately removed in this replacement: chronological finite paging, immediate intake but no promisedthree-dispatch fresh admission against arbitrary backlog. Surface catch-up accurately. This is an explicit tradeoff versus82j, not a claim that old latencyacceptance remains satisfied. No silentmessage loss: oversized message/capacity cases must expose bounded unresolved-overflow with canonicalref; advance without semantics only where documented.

Use code-assigned taskIDs, exact canonicalsource refs, complete task-local independent status decisions. Completion is assessed post-patch, including new tasks. Done tasks need only withdrawal (not a contradictory simultaneousyes-completion question); this is a narrow intentional difference from the evaluation prototype.

Actual selectedmodelcall is ctx.modelRegistry.complete(ctx.model,...). Publicdeclarations confirmed by main locally; hostintegration must prove dispatch/auth/tool-free handling on0.84.2 and0.85.1. Hosthint alone does not bound a transport ignoring timeout/abort: controller must own deadline/epoch and staleadmission protection. No credentials copied or manually lookedup; no recursiveagentsession.

Read-only peer study reinforces deterministic reducer/provider-adapter split and explicit degradation. No scope additions; do not adopt its unbounded parallelbatch or weak abort/resume semantics.

## Definition of done

Beads carry portable full plan, issue-specific scope, acceptance, tests and ownership; private ignored task paths supplement rather than replace issue bodies. Close each issue only after main verifies its slice. H5 includes independent full diff since lastacceptedafdbee79, so inherited26b60a33 repairs are not treated as alreadyreviewed. Reconcile outstanding82j.5/.5.1/.6 explicitly at finalacceptance; do not close them as delivered before equivalent safety work is accounted.

No nudges/advisory/debugger, no new UI project, no compatibilitylayers or automaticLLMrepairs. All costs/errors retained, bounded serial paid QA afteroffline gates. A miss of a gating fixture alreadyaccepted byuser is recorded aslimitation; do not lowerthresholds to pass it. Completion practicalminimum for CI remains≥2/3;3/3desired, not newly imposedperfectrecall. Exact initialCI must yield usable grounded breakdown. Gate/LLM/transport/controller outcomes distinguished.


## Planner architecture (amendments above prevail)

# Pragmatic hybrid progress redesign — demo plan

## Goal
Replace span/scope inference with smallest passive hybrid pipeline that can demo useful stable task progress tonight: canonical message → Jev gate → host-selected-model patch when needed → independent focused completion/withdrawal → display.

## Fixed Decisions
- Focused completion evaluation already passed practical trigger: 54/57 detections, 0/90 false completions, 6/6 withdrawals, CI 3/3. No more gate/completion research before implementation.
- Demo target, not production claim. Known confident Jev gate false negatives remain accepted cost/latency tradeoff and must stay visible in live results.
- Main first creates detailed dependency Beads from this plan, then owns/freeze-commits each red-test slice. One source writer implements slices sequentially. User manual testing happens only after all automated/live gates pass.
- No v4 migration, manual source selection, checklist adapter, interval controls, nudges, injected messages, recursive agent session, model repair loop, or dashboard redesign.
- Keep `/progress`, `/progress on`, `/progress off`; keep read-only Beads enrichment.

## Runtime Contract
1. `context`, `turn_end`, and `agent_settled` expose canonical active-branch entries. Ignore raw pre-append `message_end`, tool results, custom entries, monitor entries, aborted/error messages, and excluded content.
2. Process user/assistant observations in branch order. Commit cursor only after one observation transaction settles. Duplicate hooks see same `(entryId, sha256(text))` and do no paid work.
3. Send whole bounded latest message, earlier-only bounded context, and active task summaries to one Jev gate question:
   - raw `changed`, `unchanged`, or `uncertain` stays recorded with confidence/probabilities;
   - confidence `>= .5` and selected probability `>= .8` accepts raw choice;
   - accepted raw `uncertain` becomes `semantic-unknown`;
   - any weak raw choice becomes distinct `threshold-abstention`;
   - only accepted `unchanged` skips extraction.
4. For changed/semantic-unknown/threshold-abstention, call current host-selected model once. Parse strict task patch; validate exact message quotes and all limits; apply atomically. Valid `unresolved:true` makes no scope mutation.
5. Build focused Jev questions from post-patch active tasks, including tasks added by this same assistant message:
   - open task: completion `yes/no/uncertain`;
   - done task: withdrawal `yes/no/uncertain` only;
   - chunk independently by Jev question/byte limits; never stop on first open/uncertain task.
6. Accepted completion marks only that task done. Accepted withdrawal reopens only that task. `no`, semantic uncertainty, and threshold abstention retain status while replacing separate latest-assessment metadata.
7. Commit observation cursor, checkpoint, and render count/focus/uncertainty. Run health only when semantic work is drained; newer canonical work preempts health.

### Patch schema
Strict exact-key JSON; no fences, repair, status, completion, or unknown fields:

```json
{
  "add": [{"label":"...","kind":"action|response","basis":"explicit|derived","quote":"..."}],
  "revise": [{"id":"task:1","label":"...","requirementsChanged":true,"quote":"..."}],
  "archive": [{"id":"task:2","quote":"..."}],
  "restore": [{"id":"task:2","label":"...","requirementsChanged":false,"quote":"..."}],
  "unresolved": false
}
```

- Code assigns IDs; model never does. New IDs are monotonic `task:<nextTaskId>` and never reused.
- `revise/restore requirementsChanged:false` retains completion but invalidates/recomputes displayed health for new wording.
- `requirementsChanged:true` preserves ID/history, increments semantic revision, reopens task, and invalidates old health/evidence binding. Same-message completion may then complete revised result.
- Archive excludes denominator without changing historical completion. Unchanged restore reuses ID/revision/status; changed restore reopens same ID.
- One task may be touched once per patch. `unresolved:true` requires all operation arrays empty.
- Each created/revised/restored label gets conservative health criterion `[label]`; no second classifier.

### Focus and parallel state
- Persist `focusTaskId` only for display/health. First active task touched in accepted patch becomes focus; retain it otherwise; clear if archived with no replacement.
- Focus never gates patching, completion, withdrawal, tools, or later tasks. Never auto-advance through first unfinished task.
- Widget keeps bounded progress/count plus one focus card and five existing health fields. Show count such as `2/3` even when focused A remains open. Show semantic uncertainty/threshold abstention honestly.

### Error behavior
- Malformed/invalid model patch: reject entirely, record visible scope failure, run completion against prior active tasks, then advance. No autonomous model repair/retry.
- Missing model/provider failure: retain ordered pending phase and known ledger; no timer loop. Resume only after `model_select`, explicit OFF/ON, or reload.
- OFF/shutdown/tree switch aborts Jev and model flight, increments epoch, and rejects late admission. ON/reload resumes durable accepted phase.
- Jev transport failure uses existing bounded backoff/Retry-After. Permanent Jev 4xx turns monitor off once.
- Oversized single observation becomes explicit unresolved-overflow and advances without semantic mutation; never truncate and pretend complete.

## Stable State, Privacy, and Bounds
Checkpoint v5 is deliberate clean break. Strictly reject v1–v4 or malformed v5 and rebuild bounded canonical history; no migration shim.

Persist:
- session-scoped source ID, committed message cursor, monotonic task counter;
- bounded generated labels, kind/basis/status/archive flag, semantic revision, focus ID, Beads display link;
- immutable create/revise/archive/restore/accepted-completion/accepted-withdrawal events;
- source refs `(entryId, messageHash, role, start, end, quoteHash)`, not full source text;
- latest raw per-task assessment separately from retained status;
- pending observation journal: accepted gate, applied patch event IDs, completion chunk index/results/request hashes;
- compact retained health card bound to task ID/revision/label, Jev/extraction usage, and actual dispatch times.

Privacy supersession: v4 could reconstruct exact labels from source spans; generated labels cannot. v5 therefore persists labels, capped at 240 characters, to preserve IDs and avoid model rebilling on reload. Never persist full messages, preceding context, prompts, raw model output, credentials, or auth headers.

Hard demo limits:
- 20 active tasks; 200 total tasks; 1,000 immutable ledger events; 512 KiB checkpoint.
- Patch maxima: add 6, revise 12, archive 12, restore 12; post-patch caps remain authoritative.
- Canonical page: 64 messages / 256 KiB; continue finite pages via cursor, never retain unbounded queue.
- Latest whole message: 12 KiB; preceding context: latest 2 earlier messages / 4 KiB total.
- Jev: existing 24 KiB request, 20 questions, 128 KiB response, 10 s deadline, unchanged model/thresholds.
- Extraction: input <=24 KiB; active tasks plus newest archived tasks fitting 8 KiB; output `maxTokens: 2048` and <=32 KiB text.
- Older archived tasks outside extraction context remain preserved but cannot be restored by that observation; expose unresolved instead of guessing.
- At capacity, refuse new semantic mutation visibly. Never evict IDs/evidence silently.

description:
# Approved full UX and subsequent beautification
Implement the full approved functional plan first, freeze exact build for user manual QA, then beautify while the user tests. All work remains unstarted; this turn only creates backlog. Native parent-child containment, explicit child dependency DAG. No epic-to-child reverse blocking edges.

## Execution contract
Planning/backlog only in creation turn. Implement only after coordinator releases work. Main agent owns all failing tests and test/config edits; source subagents must stop for missing tests, not write them. Do not run memo as a subagent. Use jj, no new/switch branches; one writer per cwd; each logical slice its own conventional commit. Run targeted tests and batch make format, make check, make test in order; paid/live groups separate. No migration/compatibility layer, historical rebilling, task editing, advisory or completed-cycle reset.
Pin accepted root runtime before coding: latest owner report124ee557/docs6cc4005e, 347unit+12local/global12 gates passed but cumulative review still pending. Those are candidate refs, NOT accepted base. Root owner controls existing repair issues6qv/xkg/82j; do not change their statuses. Coordinate before integrating new issue JSONL, preserving root's newer records.
UI is passive: selection, render, resize, board/debugger never reads canonical history, persists monitor state, dispatches inference, retries or adds polling. Focus is not completion/evidence/tool ownership; board selection is local. Optional enrichment cannot block mandatory tracking. Existing bounds must be re-inventoried against accepted runtime.
Source plan: .agents/plans/20260919T224144--progress-widget-board-redesign__planning/plan.md. Sequencing addendum: .agents/plans/20260919T234920--ux-backlog-polish-sequencing__planning/plan.md. Full relevant requirements are copied below so ticket remains usable without private files.
Deliver handoff with exact ref, changed files, red→green commands/results, residual risks, and artifact paths. Never claim real-host or live validation from mocks.

## 1. Product contract

### Widget

Place named widget **below the editor**. Ready/current, unselected state has two data rows plus discoverability hint:

```text
Reported 7/12 · 58%  ███████░░░░░  Jev 10:03:12
Current Task: (OPEN|INPROG|DONE) Handle escaped delimiters in parser
→ to inspect
```

Right selects it, under the safe input conditions below. Selection reveals:

```text
Jev · ↓ 10.4K · ↑ 765 tokens · 200 calls • Extraction · ↓ 1425 · ↑ 194 tokens · 20 calls
enter to see board
```

Down = input, up = output. No token usage when unselected. Proposed formatting: integers below 10,000, one-decimal K above; test rounding boundaries. Add selected-only `Enter: task board · Left/Esc: back` hint where space permits. Enter opens board. Left/Esc returns selection to editor; ordinary typing deselects and passes through.

Count is reported task completion, not correctness/effort. Compute 12-cell fill directly from done/total, independently of integer percentage. No invented minimum fill. Empty/unresolved scope gets no percentage/bar. Task identity follows accepted assistant/tool activity, never first unfinished or newest as a focus heuristic.

### Task board

A **bounded modal**, not full-height. Approximate 40/60 split, inspired by screenshot and beads_viewer: dense selected task row left, readable headings/wrapped details right. No priorities, graph analysis, assignees, exports or task mutations.

Left: **all retained tracked tasks**, newest admission first; completed/archived included with distinct status. Newest means immutable admission order, not last update. Scroll/paginate viewport without truncating logical list. Existing retention/capacity limits remain explicit; no unlimited-history promise.

Right: tracked label/identity and lifecycle metadata always visible, followed by:

```text
Summary:
• Requirements: mostly clear
• Acceptance: explicit
• New red test: Not needed
• Red evidence: Not needed
• Implementation: Not needed
```

Actual assessment values only—these example values are not defaults. Unassessed tasks show all five fields as `Unassessed`, distinct from an assessed `Unknown`/`unverified`. Include assessment time and retained/stale/replacement-pending provenance. Optional Task Title, Description and Acceptance Criteria sections appear only with grounded, confidence-accepted fields. The tracked label is always available even when richer title is omitted.

Controls proposed: Up/Down select tasks; PageUp/PageDown/Home/End navigate list; Left/Right or Tab switches active pane; arrows/pages in right pane scroll details. `d` in right pane toggles selected-task Debugger section; Esc closes modal, optional q alias. Footer shows controls. Selection stays on task ID as live state changes; activity highlighting does not move the user's selection.

### Debugger

Only inside right task pane, behind `d`. No standalone debugger modal/command. Show safe task-linked transition facts and assessment provenance. Session-wide processing/service/aggregate counters, if shown here, must be explicitly marked **Session-wide**, not attributed to selected task. No raw prompts, replies/errors, branch content, source IDs/hashes, credentials or tool payloads. Ordinary service/blocking warnings remain visible without debugger.

## 3. Architecture and invariants

[tag:ux_passive_views] One UI controller owns cached detached snapshots, below-editor component, input subscription, modal handle and local selection/scroll/debug state. Committed monitor publication updates both surfaces. Opening/rendering/navigation/resize/closing never reads canonical history, persists monitor state, dispatches inference, retries or schedules polling.

[tag:ux_focus_not_evidence] Assistant semantic focus is reused from accepted root. Additional tool activity focus is a display judgment only: no task admission, completion, health ownership, EvidenceLink, or mutation of semantic focus. Board selection is a third, view-local concept.

[tag:ux_optional_isolation] Optional details, health retention and activity analysis have independent failure/capacity outcomes. They must not stall mandatory admission/completion/cursor commit or set semantic global capacity limit.

[tag:ux_owned_overlay] Capture host TUI through widget factory; use `tui.showOverlay(component, options)` and retain its exact handle. Close via that handle's `hide()`, not `ctx.ui.custom({overlay:true})`, generic hideOverlay, or another extension's handle. Component disposal is idempotent and owned separately; no host custom-UI promise exists to strand.

### Input and lifecycle

Activation predicate: enabled TUI widget, board closed, no competing overlay, known main editor focused, no configured custom editor, editor text exactly empty, pipeline-visible non-release Right. Capture editor identity only at a proven host point; unknown identity means do not intercept. `getEditorComponent()` is factory access, not a direct editor instance getter. Host proof must establish reliable identity; never infer it by arbitrary method names.

Right means input **as received after earlier listeners**. Host does not expose original key/priority: another extension transforming keys can affect this. Tests cover both listener orders; pass-through preserves received data, not an impossible original-byte guarantee. Do not register globally unconditional bare Right shortcuts.

While selected: Enter opens one board; Right no-op; Left/Esc deselect; other input deselects and passes through. Loss of focus/empty-editor/overlay preconditions clears selection. Board captures keys only while its exact handle is focused.

Session replacement, successful branch change, OFF, reload, shutdown: invalidate generation; remove owned widget/listener; hide exact board handle and dispose once. Cancelled navigation leaves board intact. Stale publications/results cannot touch new generation. Closing a lower board while another overlay is above must preserve that overlay and focus. If supported host cannot prove these contracts, stop for owner/host decision; no fallback editor replacement/fullscreen shell without approval.

### Normal warnings and small terminals

Ready fixture stays exact. Non-ready first-row priority: unsupported/corrupt restore → semantic capacity block → unresolved/previous scope → catch-up → service unavailable → retry/analysis waiting → ready. Keep two task-data rows plus discoverability hint; drop bar before warning, then percentage, never relabel historical progress current. Bound/clamp fields by display columns; tiny widths use short truthful status, not misleading fragments.

Board shows global service/blocking banner outside Debugger. Summary shows safe assessment time/provenance beside all five labels. Unknown is not failure; provider failure does not alter task judgment. Selected token line may wrap on narrow terminals. Modal proposed width 94%, max-height 80%, centered, one-cell margin. Exact options/minimum size proven on host. At unusable dimensions show explicit size notice with functional Esc; do not silently remove health dimensions.


# Approved UX backlog and beautification sequencing

User approved UX plan and asks for detailed Beads, not runtime implementation in this turn.

Source: `.agents/plans/20260919T224144--progress-widget-board-redesign__planning/plan.md`, including pre-existing hint edits preserved in parent jj change95996db3.

1. Create one native parent epic and detailed dependency-ordered child tasks covering complete functional A0–D plan, test-first ownership and exact acceptance evidence.
2. Full functional version includes tool focus AND confidence-gated rich details before manual-QA handoff. Earlier possibility of deferring rich details no longer defines the full-plan handoff.
3. After accepted functional handoff, allow user manual testing and optional visual polish work concurrently. Never mutate the exact manual-QA build in place; preserve revision/load instructions and identify polished candidate separately.
4. Beautification: theme-aware contrast/color/spacing first; bounded optional animation only if host proof shows no inference/history/persistence side effects, no artificial progress, no blocking input, no leaked redraw timers. Honor reduced-motion setting; static default unless user chooses otherwise. Do not animate health or interpolate task completion. Unicode block glyphs are not ASCII; supply documented plain fallback where needed, not guessed terminal detection.
5. Existing plan adds `→ to inspect` and `enter to see board`: treat as discoverability requirement. Two data rows plus explicit hint row by default; selected state adds requested usage and enter hint. Reconcile stale exact-two-total-rows wording in implementation docs/tests; do not delete supplied hints.
6. Beads native parent-child only for containment; blocking edges only among work items. No reverse epic→child blocking edges.
7. Verify descriptions/acceptance coverage and dependency graph; independent full-backlog review; sync and commit. No implementation, test execution, provider calls or branch changes.

## Owner amendment: visible task status (functional requirement)
User explicitly requires `Current Task: (OPEN|INPROG|DONE) Handle escaped delimiters in parser`. Parentheses contain ONE actual status, not the literal alternatives. Status text ships in the complete simple/functional build. Color is desirable, not a prerequisite; P01 applies theme-aware status color during polish.
[tag:ux_task_status_truth] Display status is a typed projection, not mutation of semantic state. Mapping must be frozen/tested at U00: included reported-done task => DONE; included open task with currently accepted exclusive activity/semantic-focus evidence => INPROG; other included open/reopened task => OPEN. INPROG is reported activity, not evidence of completion, and stale/pending/uncertain focus must not keep falsely current INPROG. Archived status stays distinct in board; never coerce archive to DONE. No confident task => explicit not-identified/multiple/pending text, not fabricated OPEN task.
Ensure DONE actually has a reachable widget state: after exact displayed task completes, preserve its identity as explicitly idle/last-reported DONE while no newer work/evidence supersedes it. Never substitute arbitrary first/newest task. New user/tool work, source/task revision, unresolved scope or unknown/concurrent judgment must invalidate/requalify that retained display; do not keep stale DONE as current activity. Freeze exact short idle/retained qualifier in U00 alongside owner's Current Task prefix. Do not alter durable status or denominator to render this.
Main tests OPEN→INPROG→DONE, reopen→OPEN, focus switches, completion while pending, idle retained DONE, new work superseding DONE, unknown/concurrent, archived tasks and same-label revisions. Text remains visible monochrome; optional colors never turn reported DONE into verified-success claim or conceal warnings. U05/U06 project identity/status safely; U07/U08 render it; U11/U12 enforce focus freshness; P01 theme-polishes it.

Place named widget **below the editor**. Ready/current, unselected state has two data rows plus discoverability hint:

```text
Reported 7/12 · 58%  ███████░░░░░  Jev 10:03:12
Current Task: (OPEN|INPROG|DONE) Handle escaped delimiters in parser
→ to inspect
```

Right selects it, under the safe input conditions below. Selection reveals:

```text
Jev · ↓ 10.4K · ↑ 765 tokens · 200 calls • Extraction · ↓ 1425 · ↑ 194 tokens · 20 calls
enter to see board
```

Down = input, up = output. No token usage when unselected. Proposed formatting: integers below 10,000, one-decimal K above; test rounding boundaries. Add selected-only `Enter: task board · Left/Esc: back` hint where space permits. Enter opens board. Left/Esc returns selection to editor; ordinary typing deselects and passes through.

Count is reported task completion, not correctness/effort. Compute 12-cell fill directly from done/total, independently of integer percentage. No invented minimum fill. Empty/unresolved scope gets no percentage/bar. Task identity follows accepted assistant/tool activity, never first unfinished or newest as a focus heuristic.

### Task board

A **bounded modal**, not full-height. Approximate 40/60 split, inspired by screenshot and beads_viewer: dense selected task row left, readable headings/wrapped details right. No priorities, graph analysis, assignees, exports or task mutations.

Left: **all retained tracked tasks**, newest admission first; completed/archived included with distinct status. Newest means immutable admission order, not last update. Scroll/paginate viewport without truncating logical list. Existing retention/capacity limits remain explicit; no unlimited-history promise.

Right: tracked label/identity and lifecycle metadata always visible, followed by:

```text
Summary:
• Requirements: mostly clear
• Acceptance: explicit
• New red test: Not needed
• Red evidence: Not needed
• Implementation: Not needed
```

Actual assessment values only—these example values are not defaults. Unassessed tasks show all five fields as `Unassessed`, distinct from an assessed `Unknown`/`unverified`. Include assessment time and retained/stale/replacement-pending provenance. Optional Task Title, Description and Acceptance Criteria sections appear only with grounded, confidence-accepted fields. The tracked label is always available even when richer title is omitted.

Controls proposed: Up/Down select tasks; PageUp/PageDown/Home/End navigate list; Left/Right or Tab switches active pane; arrows/pages in right pane scroll details. `d` in right pane toggles selected-task Debugger section; Esc closes modal, optional q alias. Footer shows controls. Selection stays on task ID as live state changes; activity highlighting does not move the user's selection.

### Debugger

Only inside right task pane, behind `d`. No standalone debugger modal/command. Show safe task-linked transition facts and assessment provenance. Session-wide processing/service/aggregate counters, if shown here, must be explicitly marked **Session-wide**, not attributed to selected task. No raw prompts, replies/errors, branch content, source IDs/hashes, credentials or tool payloads. Ordinary service/blocking warnings remain visible without debugger.

## 3. Architecture and invariants

[tag:ux_passive_views] One UI controller owns cached detached snapshots, below-editor component, input subscription, modal handle and local selection/scroll/debug state. Committed monitor publication updates both surfaces. Opening/rendering/navigation/resize/closing never reads canonical history, persists monitor state, dispatches inference, retries or schedules polling.

[tag:ux_focus_not_evidence] Assistant semantic focus is reused from accepted root. Additional tool activity focus is a display judgment only: no task admission, completion, health ownership, EvidenceLink, or mutation of semantic focus. Board selection is a third, view-local concept.

[tag:ux_optional_isolation] Optional details, health retention and activity analysis have independent failure/capacity outcomes. They must not stall mandatory admission/completion/cursor commit or set semantic global capacity limit.

[tag:ux_owned_overlay] Capture host TUI through widget factory; use `tui.showOverlay(component, options)` and retain its exact handle. Close via that handle's `hide()`, not `ctx.ui.custom({overlay:true})`, generic hideOverlay, or another extension's handle. Component disposal is idempotent and owned separately; no host custom-UI promise exists to strand.

### Input and lifecycle

Activation predicate: enabled TUI widget, board closed, no competing overlay, known main editor focused, no configured custom editor, editor text exactly empty, pipeline-visible non-release Right. Capture editor identity only at a proven host point; unknown identity means do not intercept. `getEditorComponent()` is factory access, not a direct editor instance getter. Host proof must establish reliable identity; never infer it by arbitrary method names.

Right means input **as received after earlier listeners**. Host does not expose original key/priority: another extension transforming keys can affect this. Tests cover both listener orders; pass-through preserves received data, not an impossible original-byte guarantee. Do not register globally unconditional bare Right shortcuts.

### Normal warnings and small terminals

Ready fixture stays exact. Non-ready first-row priority: unsupported/corrupt restore → semantic capacity block → unresolved/previous scope → catch-up → service unavailable → retry/analysis waiting → ready. Keep two task-data rows plus discoverability hint; drop bar before warning, then percentage, never relabel historical progress current. Bound/clamp fields by display columns; tiny widths use short truthful status, not misleading fragments.

Board shows global service/blocking banner outside Debugger. Summary shows safe assessment time/provenance beside all five labels. Unknown is not failure; provider failure does not alter task judgment. Selected token line may wrap on narrow terminals. Modal proposed width 94%, max-height 80%, centered, one-cell margin. Files: `analysis/extractor.ts`, new `analysis/task-details.ts`, state/checkpoint/proof/monitor, board projection; parser/grounding/detail/replay/admission tests.

Never substitute arbitrary first/newest task. Freeze exact short idle/retained qualifier in U00 alongside owner's Current Task prefix. Do not alter durable status or denominator to render this.

U05/U06 project identity/status safely; U07/U08 render it; U11/U12 enforce focus freshness; P01 theme-polishes it.

Implement storage, jobs, confidence validation, projection and renderer behind a DISABLED rich-section gate. U15 closes when disabled implementation and U14 red→green coverage pass; it does not authorize user-visible rich sections. Test-only fixtures can exercise enabled paths without enabling production display. U16 owns real calibration, policy acceptance, fixes and final enablement. No user-facing rich title/description/criteria before U16 acceptance; tracked label and five-field Summary remain usable.

## Ownership
main-coordinator. Test-first handoff mandatory for source writes.

## Acceptance and verification
User receives stable named functional build and checklist; all planned behaviors included; evidence/ref/limitations recorded. Beautification can begin without waiting for user manual QA completion.

Planning/backlog only in creation turn. Implement only after coordinator releases work. Main agent owns all failing tests and test/config edits; source subagents must stop for missing tests, not write them. Do not run memo as a subagent. Use jj, no new/switch branches; one writer per cwd; each logical slice its own conventional commit. Run targeted tests and batch make format, make check, make test in order; paid/live groups separate. No migration/compatibility layer, historical rebilling, task editing, advisory or completed-cycle reset.

Those are candidate refs, NOT accepted base. Root owner controls existing repair issues6qv/xkg/82j; do not change their statuses. Coordinate before integrating new issue JSONL, preserving root's newer records.
UI is passive: selection, render, resize, board/debugger never reads canonical history, persists monitor state, dispatches inference, retries or adds polling. Focus is not completion/evidence/tool ownership; board selection is local. Optional enrichment cannot block mandatory tracking. Existing bounds must be re-inventoried against accepted runtime.

## 1. Product contract

### Widget

Place named widget **below the editor**. Ready/current, unselected state has two data rows plus discoverability hint:

```text
Reported 7/12 · 58%  ███████░░░░░  Jev 10:03:12
Current Task: (OPEN|INPROG|DONE) Handle escaped delimiters in parser
→ to inspect
```

Right selects it, under the safe input conditions below. Selection reveals:

```text
Jev · ↓ 10.4K · ↑ 765 tokens · 200 calls • Extraction · ↓ 1425 · ↑ 194 tokens · 20 calls
enter to see board
```

Down = input, up = output. No token usage when unselected. Proposed formatting: integers below 10,000, one-decimal K above; test rounding boundaries. Add selected-only `Enter: task board · Left/Esc: back` hint where space permits. Enter opens board. Left/Esc returns selection to editor; ordinary typing deselects and passes through.

Count is reported task completion, not correctness/effort. Compute 12-cell fill directly from done/total, independently of integer percentage. No invented minimum fill. Empty/unresolved scope gets no percentage/bar. Task identity follows accepted assistant/tool activity, never first unfinished or newest as a focus heuristic.

### Task board

A **bounded modal**, not full-height. Approximate 40/60 split, inspired by screenshot and beads_viewer: dense selected task row left, readable headings/wrapped details right. No priorities, graph analysis, assignees, exports or task mutations.

Left: **all retained tracked tasks**, newest admission first; completed/archived included with distinct status. Newest means immutable admission order, not last update. Scroll/paginate viewport without truncating logical list. Existing retention/capacity limits remain explicit; no unlimited-history promise.

Right: tracked label/identity and lifecycle metadata always visible, followed by:

```text
Summary:
• Requirements: mostly clear
• Acceptance: explicit
• New red test: Not needed
• Red evidence: Not needed
• Implementation: Not needed
```

Actual assessment values only—these example values are not defaults. Unassessed tasks show all five fields as `Unassessed`, distinct from an assessed `Unknown`/`unverified`. Include assessment time and retained/stale/replacement-pending provenance. Optional Task Title, Description and Acceptance Criteria sections appear only with grounded, confidence-accepted fields. The tracked label is always available even when richer title is omitted.

Controls proposed: Up/Down select tasks; PageUp/PageDown/Home/End navigate list; Left/Right or Tab switches active pane; arrows/pages in right pane scroll details. `d` in right pane toggles selected-task Debugger section; Esc closes modal, optional q alias. Footer shows controls. Selection stays on task ID as live state changes; activity highlighting does not move the user's selection.

### Debugger

Only inside right task pane, behind `d`. No standalone debugger modal/command. Show safe task-linked transition facts and assessment provenance. Session-wide processing/service/aggregate counters, if shown here, must be explicitly marked **Session-wide**, not attributed to selected task.
